title: This human body is your chance
hookLine: bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa: you have this human body; now is your chance (Asa M5, ang 12)

cards: A crowded government office. You took a paper ticket an hour ago: number 147. The screen says 139.
You scroll your phone, check the time, scroll again. 143. You go to get water.
145. You answer a message from your cousin. And then you look up and the screen says 149, and a voice is calling a number that isn't yours anymore.
Your turn came, and passed, while you were looking somewhere else. Guru Arjan uses that very idea, a turn.

teach.b: The fourth So Purakh shabad is by Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru. It opens: bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa. You have received this human body.
Then: gobind milan kee eh teree bareeaa. This is your turn to meet the Lord of the universe.

teach.h: BAREEAA: YOUR TURN TO MEET THE LORD.
teach.b: Bareeaa is a turn, like a turn in a queue, or your turn at the well.
Sikh teaching speaks of the soul passing through many lives, and of a human birth as rare and precious, the one in which a person can consciously remember the One.
So the shabad says, in paraphrase: other work won't help you here. Join the company of the holy and meditate on the Name alone.
Put your effort into crossing the frightening ocean of the world; your life is slipping away in the color of maya. Notice it doesn't say other work is evil.
Sikhs work, raise families and run businesses; Sikh tradition remembers Guru Arjan building the Harmandir Sahib.

teach.h: OTHER WORK CAN'T DO THIS ONE JOB.
teach.b: It says other work can't do this particular job. Then, like Guru Nanak yesterday, Guru Arjan turns humble. I haven't practiced meditation, austerity, self-control or right living, he says.
I haven't served the holy or known the Lord.

teach.h: MY DEEDS ARE LOWLY; I SEEK YOUR SHELTER.
teach.b: Nanak says: my deeds are lowly. I have come to Your shelter; protect my honor.
So the chance isn't something to earn by being impressive. It's a turn that's already come. The number on the screen is yours, right now.

how: Bhaee paraapat is the last shabad of the So Purakh group in Rehras Sahib, recited each evening; its opening line is quoted in Sikh teaching about the preciousness of human life.

o: a soul between one life and the next
an angel sent down to guide people
human: this human life, your turn

p: the fifth Guru, the voice of this shabad

s: the shabad says all ordinary work is sinful
it says other work can't do this one job; Sikhs work, raise families and build.
Sikh teaching sees a human birth as rare and precious
the life in which a person can consciously remember the One.
Guru Arjan claims great spiritual achievements in this shabad
he says his deeds are lowly and seeks shelter at the Lord's door.

games.q: you're told your turn has come: this human life is your chance to meet the Lord. what does the shabad tell you to do?
o: join the company of the holy and remember the Name.
work harder at everything else first.
games.why: Guru Arjan says other work can't do this job: meet with the sangat and meditate on the Name, now, while it's your turn.

practice: Bring to mind one good thing you've been meaning to do, a call to someone lonely, an apology, a thank-you note, something small enough to start today, and picture yourself doing it.
Then rest with the breath and the line: this is your turn. If you pray, you can say Waheguru once.

wordCard.voice: Maanukh, human: Guru Arjan says this human life is your turn to meet the Lord, so don't let it pass.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: maanukh, human; bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa, you have received this human body.

carryVoice: Your line: now is the chance. A human life is the turn. See you tomorrow.
